title: When does a pond fill fastest?
hook: More fish make more babies. So is a nearly full pond growing fastest?

knows: a habitat can only hold so many animals
doesNotKnow: that growth in numbers is fastest at half the carrying capacity

misconception: A population grows fastest when it is nearly full, because that is when it has the most members having young.
objective: The learner can explain that logistic growth needs both individuals and room, so new individuals per unit time (rN(1 - N/K)) peak at half the carrying capacity, where the S-curve bends.

claims.text: In the logistic model, growth per unit time is r x N x (1 - N/K): it needs both individuals (N) and room left (1 - N/K).
claims.source: Verhulst (1838); Gotelli, N. J., A Primer of Ecology (Sinauer), ch. 2, logistic population growth.

claims.text: With r = 0.5 per month and K = 1,000: 45 new fish per month at 100 fish, 45 at 900 and 125 at 500.
Logistic growth in numbers is fastest at half the carrying capacity (500 here), which is where the S-curve bends from speeding up to slowing down.
claims.source: d/dN [rN(1 - N/K)] = r(1 - 2N/K) = 0 at N = K/2; the maximum of dN/dt is the inflection point of N(t).

claims.text: Real populations can lag behind, overshoot their limit or crash, unlike this model.
claims.source: Gotelli, A Primer of Ecology, ch. 2 (time lags in logistic growth); May, R. M. (1976), 'Simple mathematical models with very complicated dynamics', Nature 261: 459-467.

claims.text: The pond, its growth rate (0.5 per month) and its fixed 1,000-fish limit are made up.

recall.question: A range can support at most 2,000 deer, and the herd grows logistically. At what herd size does it add deer fastest?
recall.why: Growth needs deer and room; deer x room-left peaks at half the limit, 1,000.
